question: Drug of choice for relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis is:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis" -> "requires disease-modifying therapy" -> "Beta IFN is a first-line treatment" -> "widely accepted in clinical guidelines" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis" -> "treatment options include various immunomodulators" -> "Natalizumab is effective for severe cases" -> "not first-line for all patients" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis" -> "Beta IFN reduces relapse rates" -> "improves long-term outcomes" -> "considered standard of care" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis" -> "Gamma IFN is not commonly used" -> "less evidence for efficacy" -> "not preferred" -> 80%
analysis: In the management of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS), the primary goal is to reduce the frequency of relapses and slow disease progression. Beta interferons (Beta IFN) are well-established as first-line disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) for RRMS, supported by extensive clinical evidence demonstrating their efficacy in reducing relapse rates and improving long-term outcomes. While Natalizumab is effective and may be used in more severe cases or when other treatments fail, it is not considered a first-line option for all patients. Gamma interferon has limited evidence for use in RRMS and is not a standard treatment. Therefore, based on the consensus in clinical guidelines and the established role of Beta IFN as a first-line therapy, the most appropriate drug of choice for RRMS is Beta IFN.
